cases.assertion: a delivery item exposes stable identity and tenant/session/task scope without file bytes
large content is represented by an ObjectStore or Claim-Check reference rather than an event payload
an obj reference from another tenant is rejected even when the URI is syntactically valid
a delivery exceeding the configured file count limit is rejected
single-file and aggregate byte limits are checked at write and download boundaries
absolute paths, dot-dot segments, symlink escapes, reserved directories, and duplicate targets are rejected
an untrusted filename or media type cannot force browser or worker execution semantics
download requires caller identity plus tenant, session, task, and artifact authorization
an expired or revoked lease cannot be reused to download an artifact
a retry obtains fresh authorization without extending the original artifact lifetime
responses, events, SSE, logs, traces, and errors contain no secret or signing key plaintext
repeating the same delivery request returns the same confirmed items without duplicate business records
per-file ready and failed results are explicit and aggregate success cannot hide a partial delivery
cancelled or timed-out unconfirmed objects follow existing ObjectStore cleanup rules
old clients can still read the existing artifacts string list when metadata fields are added
an unknown artifact state is not interpreted as ready or downloadable
SSE replay and reconnect resend metadata or a re-fetch hint without creating another artifact
a short-lived download link is not written into durable task history or replay payloads
